meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means buddy .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means former .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means hill .

This radical is made up of blackjack and clothes with the six kanji on top. If you see six people playing blackjack and wearing the same clothes you should know that they're all nurse s. Nurses play blackjack together to cool down between shifts and they usually don't have time to change out of their uniforms. That's why this radical is nurse.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means reality .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means scroll .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means sky .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means three .

Raise your fingers to the sky to symbolize that you abstain from something. If someone offers you fur coats, raise your fingers to abstain. If someone tries to get you to bully someone, raise your fingers to abstain. Hints Abstaining from doing what other people are doing is important sometimes. So make sure you never forget the universal abstaining symbol.
readingMnemonic: This symbol to abstain comes from the hica tee ( ひか ) turtle. The hicatee is a Central American river turtle hunted for its meat, eggs, and shell. Therefore, the poor hicatee are endangered. So people started to rally around them, abstaining from hurting them anymore. They raised their fingers to the sky and shouted, "I abstain from harming these hicatee!" Hints Picture yourself in Central America. Standing in the water, blocking poachers from the hicatee turtles. "Abstain!" you shout at them.

meaningMnemonic: On your roof every evening you meet with snake s. All snakes know your address . Hints You're snake famous. Snakes go on a pilgrimage to your address every evening. Your address is passed down from snake generation to snake generation.
readingMnemonic: The snakes come to your address every night to receive the greatest gift you can give a snake: a 手 ( あて ). Hints "You only give a 手 a night. Newcomers might have a 手 or two, but some snakes who have been coming to your address for years have hundreds of 手 s. They are human hands."

meaningMnemonic: The allocate radical and the allocate kanji are the same! Hints Know your radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: If you allocate your funds correctly you'll be able to buy as many precious jew els ( じゅう ) as you want! However, jewels are expensive, so if you don't allocate any money, you won't be able to afford any. Ever. Hints Picture all the jewels you were able to buy because you allocated your funds correctly. Imagine swimming in these jewels. Like a rich duck.

meaningMnemonic: There's a tsunami coming and you can't stop the explosion of bitter ness in your mouth. You're scared. Your mouth tastes bitter and astringent . This word also means reluctant , because wouldn't you be reluctant to let a tsunami come wash you away with that bitter explosion of flavor in your mouth? Hints You're reluctant to face this bitter end at the hands of a tsunami.
readingMnemonic: With the bitter taste in your mouth, you reluctant ly gather up all of your jew els ( じゅう ) and wait for the tsunami to take you away. At least with your jewels with you, there may be some hope of selling them and building a better life if you make it. Hints Try to stuff some of the jewels into your bitter mouth before the tsunami stops you.

meaningMnemonic: A mountain branch will branch off from the rest. Hints Picture this part of the mountain, branching off from the rest, into a mysterious path of its own.
readingMnemonic: If you want to branch off from your hiking group and explore this branch of the mountain, you need a special key ( き ). Just don't get caught down there or you'll get the gui llotine ( ぎ ). Hints If you branch off from the beaten path, you need 1) access, and 2) to be really careful so you keep your head.

meaningMnemonic: You take gold in exchange for executing orders to construct a buzzer . You are a small bell maker and someone orders you to make one into a buzzer in exchange for some gold. This is how you make a living. Hints Imagine the gold, heavy in your pockets, as you construct this buzzer with your bare hands. Feel the cool metal clink around in your hands as you put it together.
readingMnemonic: Finally the buzzer is done. You’ve earned your gold. You test the buzzer and it goes rin g ( りん )! Ring! Ring! Ring! Ring ring ring ring ring! Man, that ringing is annoying but hey, that’s what buzzers do. Hints Wait, should this buzzer be buzzing or ringing? Oh well, you got your gold. It’s the client’s problem now.

meaningMnemonic: This hunk of dirt sticks out in a very odd way. Oh, wait, it's just the cape jutting out into the water below. Phew. Hints This kanji looks a lot like 崎 , and it also has the same "cape" meaning! By "cape" I mean those big hunks of land that jut out into the sea, you know?
readingMnemonic: The cape below looks just like your cy borg ( さい ). Or rather, the cyborg you once had, before you had to give him up. It's kinda cross-shaped, it has a slide part, and lots of little fleshy bits. Ah, the memories. Hints Picture the cape (the land mass that sticks out into water) but it's shaped just like your old cyborg. Weep a single tear.

meaningMnemonic: Inside this giant mouth is a person , trapped, because they're a criminal . They did something bad (they touched the mouth of another person without consent) and now they're in mouth jail for criminals. Hints Picture the criminal, trapped inside the mouth. They don't even look sorry!
readingMnemonic: The criminal is only wearing shoe s ( しゅう ). They're completely naked otherwise. They have to wear shoes because the mouth jail would be too slippery for them to stand otherwise. Hints Wearing nothing but shoes is also really uncomfortable too, so it's actually part of the criminal's punishment. They don't seem to know that though.

meaningMnemonic: When you say " Nurse !" you're probably asking to defer to them in some way, shape, or form. Hints There's many situations where you'd want to defer to a nurse, like when somebody is seriously hurt and you don't know what to do to help them. Just imagine yourself saying "Nurse!" in order to defer to them for their medical knowledge.
readingMnemonic: The reason you’re trying to defer to a nurse is because you’re trying to save the local farmhand, Joe ( じょう ). He’s seriously injured, and you don’t know how to help him, so you’ll have to defer to the knowledge of a nurse. Hints You’re starting to panic because you don’t know to help Joe, so you’re just going around saying “Nurse! Nurse!” repeatedly, desperately looking for someone you could defer to. Nurse!!!

meaningMnemonic: In through your door walks a turkey , so you employ it. You've always employed any turkey that comes through that door. Hints Imagine hundreds of turkeys walking in. The word has gotten out amongst the turkey community that if they walk through your door, you'll employ them.
readingMnemonic: Although you employ turkeys, when a 子 ( こ ) walks through your door, you send them away. Hints "I will employ turkeys, but I will never employ children!" you exclaim.

meaningMnemonic: The excuse radical and the excuse kanji are exactly the same! Dandy! Hints Know your radicals, stop making excuses.
readingMnemonic: Who always makes excuse after excuse? Men ( めん )! They have an excuse for everything. Why didn’t you take out the trash? Why did you forget my birthday? It’s just excuse after excuse with men. So I’ve heard, anyway. Hints Imagine all the men you’ve talked to in your life. Think of every excuse they’ve told you. Think of the worst excuse you’ve ever heard. Remember that.

meaningMnemonic: Your buddy the sheep is part of a flock . A flock of sheep. Your sheep buddy is a member of a flock. Hints Imagine following your sheep buddy back to his flock. Feel the soft fur of all the sheep around you as they baa peacefully.
readingMnemonic: Now take out your gun ( ぐん ) and murder every sheep in the flock . Except for your buddy. You’re incredibly jealous of your buddy and you don’t like the attention his flock gives him so that’s why you decided to murder them all with a gun. Hints Feel the recoil of the gun in your hands and the ringing of the shots in your ears as you slaughter the flock without remorse. BANG BANG BANG!

meaningMnemonic: In a tree on nine branches are some cross frame s. Each cross frame is hung on the branches of the tree. You don’t know who decided to hang the frames there, but you think it might be some new wave art or something. Actually you need a frame, and there are already nine up there, so you decide to take one. Hints Feel the tree bark under your palms as you climb up the tree to take a frame. You get a splinter from grabbing the frame. It really smarts.
readingMnemonic: You realize that the frame isn't half as nice as you thought it was, in fact it's totally wack ( わく ). How disappointing. Hints Why is this frame so wack? Think about what makes it wack, to help you remember this reading.

meaningMnemonic: Take some gold and allocate it to buy a gun . Guns are weapons of the old world, so you can't just buy them with paper money. Guns have to be bought with gold coins or bricks. Hints Picture yourself handing over an armful of gold bars to buy a single gun.
readingMnemonic: You need this gun so you can steal some jew els ( じゅう )! Why didn't you just use your gold to buy the jewels, you ask? Because! That's not how we did things in olden days. When you want jewels you buy a gun with gold and rob a jewelry store! Hints Picture an old fashioned holdup. You're holding a gun and shoveling jewels into a burlap sack. The heist of the century!

meaningMnemonic: A leader who lives in a mountain is a hermit . The only thing this hermit is a leader of now is mountain goats. This hermit dislikes people so that’s why he lives in a mountain now. Hints Imagine this odd hermit leading mountain goats around the mountain, marching to the beat of a drum. It’s a strange sight indeed.
readingMnemonic: One day the hermit was leading the mountain goats around and he ran into a cen taur ( せん ). The centaur said that he was the rightful leader of these mountain goats so the centaur challenged the hermit to a duel. Hints Picture this old hermit fighting this centaur in a duel. Who do you think is gonna win? Hear the hermit screaming in agony as the centaur demolishes him.

meaningMnemonic: There are three slide s sticking out of this building that lead to your home country . The rest of the slides go to other places, but three are yours. Hints Imagine standing at the top of the building and looking down at the three slides that stretch off toward your home country. It takes a few hours to slide all the way there, but at the end you'll be home.
readingMnemonic: Your home country is your ho me ( ほう )! Hints Even if you move, even if you haven't been back in years, your home country will always be your home in some way, deep down.

meaningMnemonic: You loiter at noon near a stop sign to get a stamp of approval from someone honorable . This honorable personage drives by at noon every day, and because they have to stop at the stop sign, people loiter here for a chance to get their honorable stamp of approval. Hints Imagine feeling nervous as the honorable person pulls up at the stop sign. Hear yourself humbly asking for their stamp as you hand the written request to them. And just who is this honorable being, anyway?
readingMnemonic: The honorable personage is Go dzilla ( ご ). Actually, you're requesting Godzilla's stamp of approval for a new demolition job in downtown Tokyo. Godzilla is the god of urban demolition, what with all those cities it's destroyed, and you need its honorable approval to continue. Hints Imagine the relief you'd feel as Godzilla hands the request back to you with its personal stamp — some kind of webbed claw print that basically blacks out the whole paper. Thank you, O honorable Godzilla.

meaningMnemonic: When someone wants to view your soul 's reality , show it with humility . Because the reality is... our souls are all a little dirty. And we haven't been the best versions we could be. So make sure when you show all of yourself you do so with some humility. Hints Focus on the feeling of humility here. You're putting it all out there, you know? With nowhere to hide.
readingMnemonic: As humility washes over you, you feel a shaking in your shin s ( しん ). Humility lives in your shins, so now they're shaking and trying to bring you down to the ground. Hints Imagine humility literally moving through your shins. Can you still stand or do you need to fall to your shins, in humility?

meaningMnemonic: Next to a tree , you find a crab playing Japanese chess (aka shogi ). Hey, why not? In New York people play chess in the park, and in Japan crabs play shogi next to a tree. Sometimes this also means go , which is a different strategic board game from China. Kind of confusing, but just think "strategic East Asian board game" and you're in the right territory for this kanji. Hints Anyway, picture this tree crab using its claws to set up the shogi pieces. It looks so experienced and confident. Then it fixes its beady, intimidating little eyes on you, raises its big claw, and makes a "come here" gesture. A challenge?
readingMnemonic: If you can beat the tree crab at a game of Japanese chess , it'll give you key ( き ). What kind of key? The key to whatever treasure you desire. Pretend you're in a crab- and shogi-based JRPG, and this crab is the final boss. A magic key is a fitting reward, right? Hints Imagine beating the crab at shogi and receiving, with due reverence, the key it bestows on you. Heft it in your hands: it's heavy and made of gold. What will you open with this key?

meaningMnemonic: You use your foot to kick Wolverine in the face so a turkey can leap to freedom. This turkey is trying to escape from Wolverine by leaping over a fence. Wolverine doesn’t want the turkey to escape, but you kick him with your foot and the turkey is then free to leap to safety. Hints Imagine kicking Wolverine in the head with your foot as the turkey makes turkey sounds in the background. He’s taller than you so you must leap as you kick.
readingMnemonic: After you kick Wolverine and the turkey is safe, you leap onto a yak ( やく ) to make your getaway. This yak is really fast so you’ll have no problem outrunning Wolverine while riding it. Hints Leap! Leap onto the yak. Feel the yak fur beneath you as you ride away to safety, wind in your hair.

meaningMnemonic: They say Mona Lisa had more modesty than any other woman at the time. Hints Leonardo da Vinci picked her for her modesty. She's so modest she shows no emotion.
readingMnemonic: The modesty of Mona Lisa inspired Ken ( けん ) the samurai to become more modest. Hints Have you met Ken the samurai in person? He never smiles, and will never show you his emotions. He's too modest for that.

meaningMnemonic: A drop of rain falls on a bear leaning up against a cross stuck into a mound . The drop wakes the bear up and he rolls down off the mound. After the bear rights himself, he assumes that the cross pushed him off the mound so he charges into the cross atop the mound and knocks it over. Hints Imagine this whole scene. A drop of water rouses the bear and he becomes enraged after he rolls down the mound. Hear the bear roar with anger as he charges up the mound and violently smashes the cross into the ground.
readingMnemonic: Once the bear fully wakes up he realizes that he just rolled down the mound on his own and the cross was not to blame. What a foo l ( ふ ) this bear was. He knows it too. The bear feels pretty foolish. Hints Now look at the bear sitting atop the mound with his head in his paws, looking like a fool filled with regret. This bear feels like a fool for attacking the cross like he did.

meaningMnemonic: The one sided radical and the one sided kanji are the same! Hints Know your radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: Think of anything that is one sided . A battle. A sports game. A relationship. What makes them so one sided? One side always has a cata pult ( かた ). Hints Imagine a one sided situation that you've had. Now imagine the winning side with a catapult. For example, a baseball game where one team is destroying the other. That's because instead of a pitcher, they have a catapult.

meaningMnemonic: Construction for geoduck s doesn't require as much paperwork as construction for humans, but you still need to write at least a paragraph to explain what you're doing. Hints Actually imagine yourself writing one paragraph of explanation to the city so you can get the permits to construct housing for your geoducks. On the form, it specifies you should only write a paragraph.
readingMnemonic: You turn in your paragraph , and it is given to Emperor こう いち , who insists on being involved in all construction projects. Surprisingly, he approves your construction project, thanks to that paragraph you wrote in the application. Hints In that paragraph, you praised こういち for being a great emperor, and you said that this construction project would help you to have more time to do your WaniKani reviews. Clearly you were pandering to Emperor こういち when you wrote it. But hey, it worked! Hint: When you see 工 in a kanji it will often take the こう reading.

meaningMnemonic: Criminal writing is always patterned . That is to say, there is a pattern to it, lots of ARGS and GONNA STAB YAs, but it's also patterned beautifully, with a collage of cut out letters. Hints Can you see the patterns in the writing this criminal did? It looks like a quilt or some plaid. It's almost beautiful, the way those death threats are arranged!
readingMnemonic: As you look closer at the patterned writing you realize that it forms the shape of an eagle ( い ). The most American bird of them all! Maybe this guy isn't a criminal after all! Hints Picture an eagle patterned out of cut out letters. What the words say isn't important (though it is asking for a ransom on your grandma), but the underlying image is gorgeous.

meaningMnemonic: A building in winter will allow life to have prosperity . Before we had buildings it was impossible to have any prosperity in winter because everything was cold and most of us died. Hints Picture a dark, bleak winter landscape. No life anywhere. Now turn around and look at the prosperity on display in the building you're in. Everyone is happy and eating food and not freezing to death.
readingMnemonic: This prosperity isn't good for everyone though. You look over and see Ryu ( りゅう ) from Street Fighter sitting in the corner. He's got everything he could ask for. He's won the tournament, he's got money, he's got this nice big building, but now he's depressed. Hints Ryu's prosperity has made him realize that having things isn't always enough. Now he's looking wistfully outside at the winter weather, missing the rough times.

meaningMnemonic: Your mouth contains a scroll , which you pull out and look at. On the scroll is a map, showing the range of the sphere of your mouth. Hints On the map, there is a circle drawn around your mouth showing what range your mouth exists in. Thankfully, your tongue and teeth are within that sphere.
readingMnemonic: Looking at the range of your mouth on the map, you notice a tiny samurai marked near your molars. It is Ken ( けん ) the samurai. Hints Everything else on the map was accurate, so you take a close look in the mirror, and there he is: a tiny Ken the samurai, protecting the range that is your mouth. He gives you a small nod and goes back to his post.

meaningMnemonic: Show your fingers to a giant to show you refuse him. Giants are very big. So big that when you talk they can't really hear what you're saying. Hold up all your fingers so that he can see what you mean. Hints Imagine holding up your fingers to show a giant you're refusing to let him do something. Yeesh, you're brave!
readingMnemonic: What do you refuse ? You refuse to let him stomp all over Little Kyo to ( きょ ). Little Kyoto is your home! And if the giant comes any closer he's going to destroy all the little buildings and shrines and soba noodle shops. Hints Imagine standing in front of a giant, refusing to let him crush Little Kyoto. I hope he doesn't stomp on you instead.

meaningMnemonic: The grain stuck in your cleat had a former life. In that life it was a rice plant . It was a happy little rice plant, minding its own business, when it was yanked up, cleaned, and put in a bag for people to buy and cook and eat. That was so long ago. Now all that's left is this sad loose grain in the bottom of your shoe. Hints When you look at a grain of rice, you should think about how it used to be a rice plant. That rice plant had a family! いいね , you think — that rice plant had a good life.
readingMnemonic: The grain of rice thinks about its former life as a rice plant and, like you, mutters " いね ." What's that, little rice grain? Are you trying to say life was good? Hints As it reminisces it wants to say "good," but the いいね is tragically cut short… much like the rice plant's life. It doesn't even have the strength to say it properly, it has to say いね . Yes, little grain, your rice plant life really was いね . Because you… were an いね . I'm sorry.

meaningMnemonic: A big turkey takes the measurement s of a safe before he can rob it. If the safe is too big it won't fit in his getaway car and the robbery will have been a failure. So before the turkey robs a place he needs to get those measurements. Hints Imagine this turkey preparing to rob a place. See him with the tape measure, and hear his little gobbles of excitement as he realizes the safe here is just the right size for robbing.
readingMnemonic: Once he's able to rob the place, he gets away in an Uber ( うば ). He just called the Uber in advance and had it wait outside. Hey, if you're gonna rob a place, make sure you have an Uber. Hints Picture this turkey with all the stuff he robbed, looking nervously over his shoulder from the back seat of his Uber.

meaningMnemonic: You come across a gold hill . You think you hit it big! You start digging, only to find out that it is merely a paper-thin layer of gold covering a hill of steel . Hints Dig out many other spots. Every time, it's just steel under there.
readingMnemonic: You report your findings about the steel you found to Emperor こう いち . He is displeased that it is a hill of steel. Hints "I suppose I can use this steel, even if it is not a hill of gold," he says. "We will make steel weapons, which we will use to subjugate other nations. The whole world will learn kanji using the WaniKani system!"

meaningMnemonic: The moon has gotten awfully heavy due to swelling . You're not sure what's caused the moon's swelling, but you hope it's just allergies and not a tumor or something. Hints Imagine looking up into the night sky and seeing an inflamed, swollen-looking moon. Poor guy.
readingMnemonic: When people see the moon's swelling , they yell: " Hah ( は )! Serves you right!" It turns out a lot of people think the moon is kind of a pompous jerk, smugly lording over everyone from the heavens, so they're happy to see it looking all swollen and uncomfortable Hints Imagine everyone gleefully yelling "Hah!" and taunting the poor, swollen moon: "Hah! Enjoy your swelling, moon! Hah! Maybe this'll teach you some humility!"

meaningMnemonic: The turtle shell radical and the turtle shell kanji are exactly the same! Oddly, this can also be used to talk about the first item in a list, so to mean A out of A through D, for example. Hints Cowabunga! You get an A!
readingMnemonic: With a turtle shell on his back, imagine こう いち . Hints Because this is WaniKani, こういち has probably set the turtle shell on fire, too. "Burn those turtle shells, burn those kanji!" he yells.

meaningMnemonic: A tiger , clad in spikes , exists in the void . This tiger is from another dimension where tigers rule the earth, clad in armor with spikes. The void has allowed this tiger to cross dimensional planes. Hints Tigers are pretty intimidating just on their own, let alone with spikey armor. Imagine this tiger, covered in spikes. It’s roaring at you. Pretty scary, huh?
readingMnemonic: The aforementioned void has opened up in Little Kyo to ( きょ ). The spiked void tigers chose to come here in order to face off against the Hanshin Tigers baseball team in battle. It will be a vicious match here in Little Kyoto. Since this is taking place in Little Kyoto and not Japan itself, the Hanshin Tigers won't have the home field advantage. Who will win? Hints Picture this grand match taking place in Little Kyoto. Actual tigers versus the Hanshin Tigers. It’s truly a sight to behold. The void tigers are armed with their spikes and the Hanshin Tigers are armed with their bats. Hear the crack of wood and the roar of tigers in the air as the battle commences.

meaningMnemonic: When a spirit stop s protecting you, you'll have to go on welfare . If you can't rely on your family spirit, you'll have to have the help and protection come from somewhere else. Hints The next time you see someone on welfare, be nice. Their spirit stopped protecting them, so they need a little more help right now.
readingMnemonic: While on welfare , you have to do the only job available to you: herding shee p ( し ). Sheep can help you out when you're having a rough time. Sheep provide warmth, wool for clothes, and even food, if you wanna get dark about it. Hints If you've ever been on welfare you probably already know about the sheep.

This word is usually used to describe someone's outstanding or remarkable activity in a certain sport, career, or other field or activity. Have a look at the common word combinations for some example usages.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

meaningMnemonic: The address name is the name that's on the address, making it the addressee . This can also mean name and address . This can be used for both physical mail and email.
readingMnemonic: The reading for 宛 is the same one you learned for the kanji. The reading for 名 comes from the kun'yomi reading, which you learned in the vocabulary word 名 and 名前 . So, the reading for this word is あてな .

sentences.japanese: この宛名は間違っているみたいです。
sentences.english: It looks like there is an error in this address.

sentences.japanese: 宛名書きの仕事を任された。
sentences.english: I was entrusted with the task of writing names and addresses.

sentences.japanese: 顧客の宛名リストを紛失してしまった。
sentences.english: I lost the list of customer names and addresses.

meaningMnemonic: 遣う means "to use," so a " small use" refers to what you can do with your spending money . You're not rolling in dough over here, so you can only use your spending money on small things. Think of it like a little allowance you can use to buy baseball cards and bubblegum and stuff.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the alternate reading of 小 and 遣う 's reading. Watch out for the rendaku.

sentences.japanese: お子さんには月々お小遣いはいくら渡しているんですか。
sentences.english: How much spending money do you give your kid a month?

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 南極 means "South Pole" or the "Antarctic"? Add range onto that word and you get the region known as the Antarctic Circle .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings all three kanji. You've seen the vocab word 南極 before as well, so you should be OK with this one!

sentences.japanese: 南極圏にはペンギン以外にも動物はいるんですか？
sentences.english: Are there any animals other than penguins in the Antarctic Circle?

meaningMnemonic: 原子 is atom and 爆弾 is bomb. What is an atom bomb? An atomic bomb .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 私の家は火災保険に入っていますが、もし誰かが原子爆弾を落として、それで家が燃えちゃった場合はどうなるんでしょうか。それでも保険金は降りるんでしょうか。
sentences.english: My house has fire insurance, but what if someone drops an atomic bomb and my house catches on fire? Would I still get the insurance money?

meaningMnemonic: Something that can abstain until it's needed makes for good backup . Think about it — you don't want backup rushing in too early, right? It should abstain until the backup is actually needed. Note that 控え isn't used for spares and extras. It's more for necessary backups, like a backup player in sports, a document copy for record keeping, or a receipt stub .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading.  You learned this reading already! Good for you!

sentences.japanese: 控えの選手には誰がいたっけ？
sentences.english: Who’s the reserve player?

meaningMnemonic: A turtle shell that is patterned has much more worth than a boring non-patterned turtle shell.
